title: Adaptive attention-kernel cost model and stability heuristics
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see brittle kernel-choice behavior across mixed workloads when integrating FlashAttention v2/v3 variants. Current selector favors raw token throughput but underestimates tail jitter and memory pressure during prefill bursts, leading to occasional latency SLO regressions and OOM fallbacks.

Goal: Implement an adaptive, telemetry-driven cost model that ranks candidate attention kernels (FlashAttn v2, FlashAttn v3, hybrid emulation) per-request and per-layer. The model should account for: expected per-token latency, tail/jitter penalty, transient GPU memory footprint, quantized precision cost, and a stability penalty for kernels with recent regressions. Integrate the model with the prefill/decode scheduler so kernel selection can be budget-aware and can switch to safer kernels early in startup or burst scenarios.

Success criteria / acceptance: 
- New cost model is live behind a feature flag and can be enabled per-deployment.
- End-to-end median latency improves or remains unchanged for representative loads, 95th latency reduces by >=10% in high concurrency synthetic bursts.
- Reduction in OOM fallbacks and kernel oscillations during warmup by >=30% on our FA3 fleet.
- Automated canary checks detect regressions and auto-fallback to previous selector within 5 minutes.

Approach: 
1) Telemetry surfaces: aggregate recent per-kernel metrics (p50/p95 latency, jitter, workspace allocation, kernel failure rate) by model shape and device type. Build short windows (1m/5m) and longer windows (1h) for stability scoring.
2) Cost features: compute a composite cost = alpha*latency + beta*jitter_penalty + gamma*mem_pressure + delta*precision_penalty + epsilon*stability_penalty. Parameters tuned via offline grid search and online bandit.
3) Bandit-informed initial probe: use a contextual Thompson-sampling bandit to explore kernel choices across shapes, with conservative priors seeded from lab benchmarks. Exploration decays as confidence grows.
4) Budget hints: extend request envelope to carry a per-request latency budget and quality budget; scheduler and selector jointly pick kernel and batch size.
5) Prefill-aware kickstart: during cold prefill, bias toward low-jitter kernels; gradually allow higher-throughput kernels as KV cache warms and stability score improves.
6) Safeguards: rollout circuit breakers that trigger fallback on sudden spike in kernel failures or 95th latency exceeding configured thresholds.
7) Tests: synthetic workload sweep (short/long sequences, varied batch shapes), regression replay from production traces, and blue/green canary with gradual traffic ramp.

Artifacts / links: 
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.example.com/runtime/attn-cost-model (draft)
- Perf dashboard (canary vs baseline): https://dashboards.redwood.example.com/d/attn-cost-model/canary-compare
- PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2847
- Canary runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Cost+Model+Canary

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- How aggressive should the stability_penalty decay be? Fast decay helps recover throughput but risks oscillation on noisy signals. Proposed default: 1h half-life with ability to tighten for enterprise fleets.
- Bandit exploration vs SLO preservation: to reduce customer impact, exploration intensity should be capped per-node and per-customer.
- Memory accounting for multi-tenant GPUs: should cost model use host-wide pressure signals or only per-allocation estimates? Starting with per-allocation estimates and adding global signals as soft constraints.

Next milestones: 
- 2026-02-25: telemetry tables and dashboard prototype (done).
- 2026-03-04: cost model library and feature-flagged selector integration (in PR).
- 2026-03-10: synthetic sweep and replay tests completed (results in comments).
- 2026-03-13: canary rollout to 5% FA3 capacity (in progress).
